metadata.title: Greedy Function Approximation: A Gradient Boosting Machine (Friedman, 2001)
metadata.framework: Gradient boosting: sequential additive modeling by fitting base learners to negative gradients of the loss function in function space
metadata.source_note: Extraction based on well-known content of Friedman (2001). No arXiv version available.

nodes.name: Additive expansion model
nodes.statement: Approximate the target function as $F(\mathbf{x}) = \sum_{m=0}^{M} \beta_m h(\mathbf{x}; \mathbf{a}_m)$ where $h(\mathbf{x}; \mathbf{a})$ is a base learner (e.g., decision tree) parameterized by $\mathbf{a}$, and $\beta_m$ are expansion coefficients. The model is built greedily, one term at a time.

nodes.name: Gradient boosting (functional gradient descent)
nodes.statement: At iteration $m$, compute the negative gradient (pseudo-residuals) $r_{im} = -\left[\frac{\partial L(y_i, F(\mathbf{x}_i))}{\partial F(\mathbf{x}_i)}\right]_{F = F_{m-1}}$ for each training example $i$. Fit a base learner $h_m$ to these pseudo-residuals: $h_m = \arg\min_h \sum_{i=1}^{n} (r_{im} - h(\mathbf{x}_i))^2$. Update: $F_m(\mathbf{x}) = F_{m-1}(\mathbf{x}) + \nu \cdot \rho_m h_m(\mathbf{x})$ where $\rho_m = \arg\min_\rho \sum_i L(y_i, F_{m-1}(\mathbf{x}_i) + \rho h_m(\mathbf{x}_i))$ is a line search and $\nu \in (0,1]$ is the learning rate (shrinkage).

nodes.name: TreeBoost (gradient boosting with trees)
nodes.statement: When using $J$-terminal-node regression trees as base learners: fit the tree to pseudo-residuals $r_{im}$ to determine the tree structure (regions $R_{jm}$), then optimize leaf values separately for each region: $\gamma_{jm} = \arg\min_\gamma \sum_{\mathbf{x}_i \in R_{jm}} L(y_i, F_{m-1}(\mathbf{x}_i) + \gamma)$. This allows different step sizes per region.

nodes.name: Shrinkage (learning rate)
nodes.statement:
Scale each tree's contribution by a factor $
u \in (0,1]$: $F_m = F_{m-1} + 
u \cdot h_m$. Smaller $
u$ requires more boosting iterations but leads to better generalization through regularization.

nodes.name: Stochastic gradient boosting
nodes.statement: At each iteration, fit the base learner to a random subsample (fraction $\eta$) of the training data rather than the full dataset. This introduces randomness that reduces overfitting and improves generalization, similar to bagging.

nodes.name: Generic gradient boosting algorithm
nodes.statement: Initialize $F_0(\mathbf{x}) = \arg\min_\gamma \sum_i L(y_i, \gamma)$. For $m = 1$ to $M$: (1) compute pseudo-residuals $r_{im}$; (2) fit base learner $h_m$ to $\{(\mathbf{x}_i, r_{im})\}$; (3) line search for $\rho_m$; (4) update $F_m = F_{m-1} + \rho_m h_m$. Output $F_M$.

nodes.name: Generality of loss functions
nodes.statement: Gradient boosting works with any differentiable loss function: squared error, absolute error, Huber loss (regression); binomial deviance, exponential loss (classification). AdaBoost is a special case with exponential loss.

nodes.name: Interpretation as steepest descent in function space
nodes.statement: Gradient boosting performs steepest descent in the function space $\{F\}$. The pseudo-residual vector is the negative gradient of the empirical loss in the $N$-dimensional space of function values at training points. The base learner provides a finite-dimensional projection of this infinite-dimensional gradient.
